svg.title: FEM Poisson shared-domain graded airbox mesh and Dirichlet vs Robin boundary closures
svg.desc: Two-panel figure: (a) conforming shared-domain mesh Omega_m subset Omega_a with geometrically graded airbox layers and outer Gamma_a boundary marker; (b) numerically computed magnetostatic potential decay u(r) for a magnetized sphere in a finite airbox R_box = 2.4 a comparing exact 1/r^2 open decay against Dirichlet (u = 0) and first-order Robin (d_n u + beta u = 0) truncation error.
svg.text: FEM Poisson Airbox: Conforming Shared Domain and Outer Boundary Closures
Shared tetrahedral topology (Ωm ⊂ Ωa), outer marker selection Γa, and analytical truncation comparison of Dirichlet vs Robin closures
Conforming Graded Airbox Mesh & Boundary Operator
Shared vertices on ∂Ωm (interface faces are NOT outer Γa markers)
AR = K + β BΓa, β = c / R★
on Γa; fails closed if empty.
Energy reduction (both): Ed = −(μ0/2)∫Ωm M·Hd dV (airbox LLG nodes zeroed)
Analytical Potential Decay u(r) & Airbox Truncation Error
Normalized radial coordinate r / a (along magnetization axis)
• Dirichlet error in internal Hd: −(a/Rbox)3 (≈ −7.2% at Rbox=2.4a; −0.8% at 5a).
• Robin (c=1): +½(a/Rbox)3 error; Robin (c=2): cancels l=1 sphere dipole, leaving
O((a/Rbox)5) higher-multipole & non-spherical box residual on cubic Γa.
• Low Krylov rtol checks algebraic error only — vary Rbox, air hmax, and body hmax.
Runtime records resolved marker, R★, c, effective β = c/R★, and excluded periodic seams.
